page: The UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 50 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core and memory constraints. The AMD EPYC 9575F CPU achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier. The shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity introduce distinct bottlenecks, resulting in a weak rating for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU physics, while PassMark memory performance is rated as poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high single-core compute capabilities relative to its entry-level resource footprint, though its shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GB memory limit its suitability for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic static web serving, and simple Redis caching operations, where its high single-core execution speed can be leveraged without exhausting the constrained memory and shared CPU resources.
